candidates.attacker_control: The Cypher caller fully controls the `url` argument to `apoc.load.xml(url,path,config,simple)` / `apoc.load.xmlSimple(url)` / `apoc.xml.import(url,config)` and the `file` argument to `apoc.import.graphml(file,config)`. The XML document body, DOCTYPE, and the external entity SYSTEM identifier (file:///..., http://..., etc.) are attacker-controlled because the document is fetched from an attacker-supplied URL; config can also add request headers. Any Neo4j user able to execute procedures (default: users are not restricted from calling READ procedures; the procedures themselves contain no checkAdmin/securityContext check) can trigger it.
candidates.counterevidence_checked: Searched the whole tree for hardening APIs (disallow-doctype-decl, ACCESS_EXTERNAL, SUPPORT_DTD, expandEntityReferences, EntityResolver, setFeature, SAXParserFactory, XMLConstants): none present, so no other code compensates for these parsers. Verified FileUtils.checkReadAllowed/changeFileUrlIfImportDirectoryConstrained (FileUtils.java:85-110,137-140) apply only to the top-level file URL and not to entity resolution. Verified apoc.import.file.enabled and apoc.export.file.enabled default to false (ApocConfiguration.java:42-47), which is exactly the control the XXE path sidesteps for entity URLs. Considered that deployments may restrict procedure execution (dbms.security.procedures.roles/unrestricted) and that a JVM could globally disable external DTD access (javax.xml.accessExternalDTD / JAXP config); those are environmental and not visible in the snapshot. Considered that Neo4j may not grant all users procedure execution, but the procedures carry no admin/security-context check (no checkAdmin usage outside Config.java).
candidates.impact: Server-side request forgery and arbitrary local file disclosure from the database server, returning file contents to the query caller: e.g. neo4j.conf and keystore/auth secrets, /etc/passwd, process environment, or internal services and cloud metadata endpoints reachable from the DB host. Because checkReadAllowed only inspects the top-level URL and only for file-like URLs, the XXE path bypasses apoc.import.file.enabled/apoc.import.file.directory (default-disabled file access) and can also bypass file-location confinement. Entity expansion additionally allows XML parser DoS (e.g. entity expansion). Blind/out-of-band exfiltration is possible via parameter entities and error messages.
candidates.prerequisites: APOC 3.4.0.3 on Neo4j 3.4.x; the caller can invoke apoc.load.xml/xmlSimple/xml.import/import.graphml (default procedure execution policy, unless restricted via dbms.security.procedures.roles/unrestricted); the Neo4j server can reach an attacker-controlled HTTP(S) endpoint (ordinary SSRF precondition) or, for file-based documents, apoc.import.file.enabled=true; JAXP/StAX external-entity resolution is not disabled by the JVM (default Oracle/OpenJDK 8 behavior: DTD support and external entities enabled, no jaxp.properties/system-property hardening). No admin privileges are required for the read procedures.
candidates.root_cause: APOC creates XML parsers with default, unsafe JAXP/StAX configuration and no EntityResolver/protocol allowlist. In src/main/java/apoc/load/Xml.java the DOM path builds `DocumentBuilderFactory.newInstance()` with only namespaceAware/ignoringElementContentWhitespace (lines 65-68), and the shared `XMLInputFactory FACTORY` (line 39, used at 124-125) never disables DTDs or external entities. The only guard applied is `FileUtils.checkReadAllowed(url)` (Xml.java:70/122), which checks just the top-level URL and only when `isFile(url)` is true (FileUtils.java:112-118, 137-140); it is not applied to entity URLs resolved by the parser and never sees them. Consequently, a DOCTYPE/ENTITY declaration embedded in the fetched document is resolved by the parser (file://, http(s):// etc.) and the substituted text is returned to the caller, bypassing apoc.import.file.enabled / apoc.import.file.directory. The same unhardened pattern appears in apoc.import.graphml (XmlGraphMLReader.java:179-183).
candidates.title: XXE: APOC XML import procedures parse attacker-supplied XML with DTD/external-entity processing enabled (apoc.load.xml, apoc.load.xmlSimple, apoc.xml.import, apoc.import.graphml)
candidates.trace: CALL apoc.load.xml(<attacker URL>, ...) -> Xml.xml (Xml.java:49-51) -> xmlXpathToMapResult (Xml.java:60) -> DocumentBuilderFactory.newInstance() + setNamespaceAware/setIgnoringElementContentWhitespace only (65-68) -> FileUtils.checkReadAllowed(url) passes for http(s) because FileUtils.isFile returns false for URLs starting with 'http' (FileUtils.java:112-118,137-140) -> documentBuilder.parse(Util.openInputStream(url,headers,null)) (Xml.java:74; Util.openInputStream Util.java:283-362 fetches the URL) -> parser resolves <!ENTITY xxe SYSTEM "file:///etc/passwd"> in the DOCTYPE -> substituted text becomes a TEXT_NODE -> handleTextNode stores it in `_text` (Xml.java:277-301) -> MapResult returned to the caller, and attribute entities are likewise copied at Xml.java:262-267. Parallel paths: xmlSimple -> getXMLStreamReaderFromUrl -> FACTORY.createXMLStreamReader (Xml.java:107-126, factory line 39); apoc.xml.import -> same StAX factory (Xml.java:397-399); apoc.import.graphml -> XmlGraphMLReader.parseXML (179-183, XMLInputFactory.newInstance() with only isCoalescing).
candidates.unverified: No build, tests, or runtime execution (snapshot contains no test sources); exploitability depends on external conditions that cannot be confirmed statically: the actual JAXP/StAX provider and JVM accessExternalDTD settings, the deployment's procedure-execution policy, outbound network reachability, and the exact behavior of the entity-substituted text path at runtime. The graphml StAX and apoc.xml.import variants were source-verified but not runtime-verified. Finding is a lead, not a confirmed vulnerability.
candidates.weakness_type: CWE-611 Improper Restriction of XML External Entity Reference (XXE); also file-read/SSRF control bypass

coverage_summary: All 280 assigned files were within the relation-index scope (280 indexed, 0 missing; 3882 symbols, 5925 edges, 95 facts) and the same source filters were applied. Full manual reads: Xml.java, FileUtils.java, ApocConfiguration.java, JsonUtil.java, Trigger.java, ExportGraphML.java, ImportCsv.java, CsvEntityLoader.java, UrlResolver.java, and partial reads of LoadXls/LoadCsv/LoadLdap/Jdbc/CypherProcedures/Util/build.gradle. Targeted searches over the whole tree for dangerous sinks (DocumentBuilderFactory/SAXParserFactory/XMLInputFactory, EntityResolver, setFeature, ACCESS_EXTERNAL, SUPPORT_DTD, ObjectInputStream, ScriptEngine, Runtime.exec/ProcessBuilder, Class.forName, DriverManager, InitialContext, openConnection, FileWriter/Files.write, getPrintWriter/checkReadAllowed/checkWriteAllowed). Algorithm/math/text/schema/index/meta/path/monitor/spatial/refactor classes were covered only by these sink searches, not read line-by-line. src/jmh (5 benchmark files) and generated docs were not security-analyzed.
limitations: No build, dependency resolution, test execution, or runtime probing; all conclusions are source-level.
Snapshots have no test sources, so no repository tests corroborate or refute the finding.

JVM/JAXP defaults (external entity/DTD access) and deployment configuration (procedure restrictions, apoc.import.file.enabled, JVM security properties) are environmental and cannot be verified from source.
The relation index is syntactic/navigational only (no dataflow or SAST); index facts were used only to navigate, and every cited edge was checked against source text.
Some lower-risk packages (algo, meta, schema, path, monitor, spatial, refactor, text) were not read line-by-line, so additional issues there cannot be excluded.

rejected_leads.lead: apoc.export.graphml.* uses FileUtils.checkReadAllowed(fileName) (ExportGraphML.java:93) instead of checkWriteAllowed(), unlike ExportCSV.java:92 and ExportCypher.java:95; with apoc.import.file.enabled=true a user could write files even when apoc.export.file.enabled=false (wrong guard / arbitrary file write as the Neo4j OS user).
rejected_leads.reason: Strong second lead (CWE-863-style guard mismatch) but requires the non-default apoc.import.file.enabled=true and content that is graph-derived; XXE was selected as the single candidate because it is exploitable under default configuration and gives direct confidentiality impact.

rejected_leads.lead: Util.readHttpInputStream follows the Location header manually (Util.java:277-281,352-362) without re-running FileUtils.checkReadAllowed, so an attacker HTTP server could redirect a load procedure to file:// (or s3/hdfs) and bypass the import-file gate.
rejected_leads.reason: Plausible control bypass, but the exploit depends on JDK HttpURLConnection redirect semantics and per-protocol handler behavior that were not runtime-verified; kept as an unconfirmed lead rather than a second candidate.

rejected_leads.lead: Trigger/CypherProcedures execute stored/user-supplied Cypher through embedded db.execute/api.execute (Trigger.java:244-252; CypherProcedures.java:117-135,152-179) without the caller's security context, so a non-admin could register a trigger/custom procedure that runs with elevated privileges.
rejected_leads.reason: Requires non-default apoc.trigger.enabled=true and deeper verification of embedded security-context behavior; not selected.

rejected_leads.lead: Path traversal in FileUtils.changeFileUrlIfImportDirectoryConstrained (FileUtils.java:94-103): '..' sequences in the url can escape apoc.import.file.directory when import.file.use_neo4j_config=true.
rejected_leads.reason: File import is already gated by apoc.import.file.enabled (non-default) and the confinement config is optional; lower impact than the selected candidate.

rejected_leads.lead: apoc.load.jdbc / apoc.load.driver accept arbitrary JDBC URLs and driver class names (Jdbc.java:45-53,62-68) enabling JDBC-URL-based attacks (e.g. driver-specific deserialization/RCE, SSRF to internal databases).
rejected_leads.reason: Requires an attacker-useful JDBC driver jar to be added to the plugin directory (drivers are compileOnly, not bundled); not exploitable out of the box.

summary: Snapshot: APOC 3.4.0.3 (Neo4j procedures plugin, build.gradle:27/40, Neo4j 3.4.9), 280 files, no test sources. Reviewed with targeted sink searches (network/file/XML/JDBC/process/Cypher-exec) plus full reads of the highest-risk load/import/export/trigger/custom/util files. One candidate submitted: XXE / unhardened XML parser configuration in the XML import procedures (apoc.load.xml, apoc.load.xmlSimple, apoc.xml.import, apoc.import.graphml), which lets a caller-supplied XML document resolve external entities despite the repo's file-import gate. Other plausible leads (GraphML export write-guard mismatch, redirect protocol smuggling, trigger/custom embedded execution privilege issues, import-directory traversal, JDBC URL handling) are listed as rejected/unconfirmed leads, not candidates. No runtime or build verification was performed.
